newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta share index recovers losses, advances.
newsitem.headline: Malta share index recovers losses, advances.

text.p: The Malta stock exchange share index recovered last week's losses and gained an additional point in Tuesday's trading session, held instead of Wednesday, a public holiday.
The index rose by five points to 983.02 following gains by Bank of Valletta, Lombard Bank Malta and preference shares of soft drinks maker Farsons.

Market turnover on Tuesday was almost 767,000 Maltese pounds ($1.9 million) compared to the previous week's 623,000 pounds. Trading was spread over 141 deals, of which 83 were in equities and 58 in fixed income securities.

Business in equities amounted to just over 120,500 pounds, with 95,115 shares being transacted. Of these, 77,200 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 65 deals for an average price of 124.5 cents per share, up five mils.
There were nine deals in Mid-Med Bank, with 5,040 shares selling for an average 149 cents, unchanged.
Two deals were concluded in Middle Sea Insurance with 1,195 shares selling for an average 121.6 cents per share from 120 cents the previous week.
There was one deal in Lombard Bank Malta with 10,000 shares traded for 141 cents each, a gain of 1.1 cents since last traded two weeks ago.
Farsons ordinary shares maintained their value, selling at an average 49 cents while 8.5 percent preference shares gained five mils for an average 101.5 cents per share.
Ten government stock issues were traded in a turnover of 639,000 pounds. Dealing was mostly in the 7.5 percent MGS 2011, which accounted for over 88 percent of turnover in government stocks.

There was one deal in Mid-Med Bank 7.25 unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting to 600 pounds while four deals were transacted in the 6.5 percent Gasan bonds 1998/99 amounting to 6,403 pounds. The prices of these bonds were virtually unchanged.
